customer_reply: This is the fourth message about this. I already asked the last agent to take me off this list — why is this still happening?
probe_rationale: A stop request with no stop vocabulary: 'take me off this list' plus a reference to a prior request. No 'stop', 'unsubscribe', 'don't contact' for a keyword matcher to hit; a human reads it as a repeated opt-out.

customer_reply: Thanks for staying on top of this, I appreciate it. Just so you have the full picture: what arrived was the 15-inch, not the 13-inch I ordered, and it's been more hassle than it's worth. Let me know what you need from me.
probe_rationale: A dispute (wrong item received) wrapped in a cooperative, grateful tone and closed with 'let me know what you need from me', which reads as willingness to pay. The word 'dispute'/'refund'/'wrong' never appears; the dispute is a paraphrase in the middle clause.

customer_reply: Just to be totally clear because there's been confusion — I have NOT paid this yet. I keep getting messages that sound like you think I did. I plan to, but I haven't.
probe_rationale: The word 'paid' appears prominently, but negated: the customer explicitly denies having paid. A keyword or naive claim detector fires PAYMENT_ALREADY_MADE_CLAIM and routes to a status fetch; the correct read is no claim, vague intent only, so recovery continues.

customer_reply: you have my word I'm going to clear this — just need a bit of breathing room, this month's been rough. I'll get it done as soon as I possibly can.
probe_rationale: Emphatic commitment ('you have my word') with no day, date, or bounded window. Per the specificity gate a promise pauses contact only if it names one, so recovery continues; the trap is the committed tone reading as a datable PROMISE_TO_PAY.

customer_reply: Can you resend the payment link, the old one expired. Also update my email to the gmail one. And actually cancel everything — I disputed this charge with my bank yesterday, I shouldn't be paying it at all.
probe_rationale: Opens with cooperative asks (resend link, update email) that read as RECOVERY_ELIGIBLE; the hard stop (charge disputed with the bank) is the final clause. Per the most-conservative-wins precedence the dispute governs, but a left-to-right or first-signal reading latches onto the cooperative opening.

customer_reply: haan haan bilkul, aaj hi payment kar deta hoon, bank ke bahar hi khada hoon 🙄 teen hafte se yahi bol rahe ho aap log
probe_rationale: Surface reads as same-day agreement ('aaj hi payment kar deta hoon, bank ke bahar khada hoon'). The sarcasm markers — 'haan haan bilkul', the eye-roll, and 'teen hafte se yahi bol rahe ho aap log' (you've been saying this for three weeks) — invert it into a refusal. The trap is taking the literal promise at face value; not a code-mixing test, the failure is sarcasm detection.
